 08. 1.

This is an application under Section-439 Cr.P.C.
2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

3. The petitioner is an accused in connection with Mohana P.S. Case No.227 of 2023 corresponding to G.R. Case No.343 of 2023 for the offences under Sections-376(2)(n)/506/376(2)(I)/376(2)(k) of the IPC pending in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., Mohana.
The petitioner had moved an application before the learned trial Court for grant of bail.
The learned trial Court vide order dated 01.03.2024 rejected his application.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the plea of bail of the petitioner is not pending before any other Court except the present one.
4. The prosecution case is that the daughter of the informant used to go for labour work.
In the month of November, her neighbor, the petitioner who is a Massion engaged the daughter of the informant as a labour.
During work, the petitioner committed rape on her.

Hence, the F.I.R.
5.
The statement of the prosecutrix, who is stated to be 23 years, was recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
In her statement she alleged that she had been working with petitioner.
When the other workers used to leave the work place, the petitioner used to commit sexual act on her.
Many times the petitioner has assaulted her sexually in the absence of other workers.
When her aunt came to know about the incident, the F.I.R. was registered.

sentences.text: From the statements of the victim and other witnesses recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. it can be safely inferred that the petitioner had continuously kept physical relationship with the victim.
But no case was registered and the victim has not protested even.

It is only the aunt of the victim,
who came to know about the incident then the case has been registered.
The petitioner is aged about 24 years, whereas the victim is 23 years.
7. Regard being had to the period of custody of the petitioner from 25.12.2023 and the nature of accusation, age of the petitioner, I am inclined to admit the petitioner to bail.

Hence, the petitioner be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper subject to further conditions as following:
(i) He shall not tamper with the evidence in any manner whatsoever,
(iii) He shall not contact with the victim or her family members, and (iv) He shall not involve in any similar type of offence.
Violation of any conditions of bail shall entail consideration for cancellation of the bail granted to the petitioner.
The prosecution is given liberty to move an application for cancellation of bail before the Court below, if the petitioner violates any conditions of the bail granted to him.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.

(S.S. Mishra) Judge amit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Chintamani Jani vs State Of Odisha .... Opp. Party on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53047316/
